q: 1. DPC should be
explain: A Damp Proof Course (DPC) must be impervious to water, continuous to prevent gaps, and can be applied both horizontally (on walls) and vertically (to basement walls) to block moisture.

q: 2. The dampness in a building is due to
explain: Dampness is multi-causal: it can rise from the ground (capillary action), penetrate from the roof/walls (rain), or occur due to poor material quality or lack of DPC (defective construction).

q: 3. In case of buildings without basement, the best position for damp-proof course (DPC) lies at
explain: For buildings without basements, the DPC is placed at the plinth level to stop capillary moisture from the ground from reaching the upper walls.

q: 4. For D.P.C. at plinth level, the commonly adopted material is
explain: In standard residential construction, a layer of rich cement concrete (typically 1:2:4) mixed with a waterproofing compound is the most common and cost-effective DPC material.

q: 5. A semi-rigid material which forms an excellent impervious layer for damp-proofing, is called
explain: Mastic asphalt is a semi-rigid mixture of asphalt, mineral filler, and fine aggregate. It is heated and poured to form a completely jointless, waterproof, and durable layer.

q: 6. The damp-proof course
options: should be of good impervious material
explain: Effective damp-proofing requires a 'barrier' approach: it must be impervious, it must be continuous (no gaps), and it must cover both vertical and horizontal paths of moisture entry.

q: 7. Dampness cause
explain: Excess moisture triggers salt migration (efflorescence), chemical breakdown of paint binders (bleaching), and creates the humid environment necessary for termite infestations.

q: 8. In ordinary residential/public buildings, the D.P.C. is provided at
explain: The Damp Proof Course (DPC) is standardly placed at the plinth level to prevent capillary moisture from rising into the walls.

q: 9. D. P. C. stands for
explain: DPC stands for Damp Proof Course, a barrier of impervious material applied to prevent moisture ingress.

q: 10. The method of damp proofing in which a layer of water repellent substance is provided, between the source of dampness and part of structure, adjacent to it is known as
explain: Membrane damp proofing involves applying a water-repellent layer or sheet (like bitumen) between the source of moisture and the building.

q: 11. The DPC is provided in building in the form of
explain: DPC can be applied horizontally (at floor/plinth levels) or vertically (on basement walls) to block moisture from different directions.

q: 12. Generally DPC is provided at
explain: While vertical DPC exists, the most common application in general building construction is a horizontal layer at the plinth.

q: 13. The D. P. C. is provided at
options: just below the ground floor level
below the top most floor level
explain: DPC is usually placed at the plinth level, which is just below the ground floor level, to intercept moisture rising from the foundation.

q: 14. The pressure due to wind of velocity V is proportional to ..........
explain: Wind pressure (P) follows the formula P = 0.6V², where P is in N/m² and V is wind speed in m/s; thus, it is proportional to the square of velocity.

q: 15. The voussoirs fixed at the crown of the arch is called ..........
explain: The 'key' or 'keystone' is the central voussoir at the top of the arch that locks all other pieces into place.

q: 16. Maximum size of aggregates used in a DPC is about
explain: Damp Proof Courses (DPC) use a thin layer of concrete/mortar, requiring small aggregates, typically capped at 10mm.

q: 17. A roof which slopes in two directions is known as ..........
explain: A gable roof (or pitched roof) consists of two sloping surfaces meeting at a ridge, forming a triangle (gable) at the end walls.

q: 18. A roof which slopes in two directions and with a break in each slope is known as ..........
explain: A gambrel roof is similar to a gable roof but each side has two different slopes, with the lower slope being steeper.

q: 19. A roof which slopes in all the four directions and having flat top is known as ..........
explain: A deck roof is a hip roof where the top portion is flat instead of ending in a ridge.

q: 20. The best and the most common material to be used as damp proofing material is
explain: Bitumen is highly effective, flexible, and impermeable, making it the most common material for horizontal and vertical DPC layers.

q: 21. A roof which slopes in all four directions and with a break in each slope is known as ..........
explain: A mansard roof is a four-sided gambrel-style hip roof where each side has two slopes, providing extra room in the attic.

q: 22. Lean to roof is used generally ..........
explain: Lean-to roofs slope in only one direction and are simplest for narrow structures like sheds, verandahs, or side additions.

q: 23. The inclined supports provided in an arch constructed to receive the arch are called as
explain: A skewback is the inclined surface on an abutment from which an arch rises.

q: 24. Flat roof are particularly suitable for tropical places because
options: The top of the flat proof can be used as a terrace
All of the above are correct
explain: In tropics, flat roofs provide outdoor space, help regulate heat through thermal mass, and allow for easy future expansion.

q: 25. Pitched roofs are particularly suitable in hilly regions because
options: It is very easy to repair
of heavy rain fall and snow fall
all of the above are correct
explain: Steep slopes allow rain and snow to shed quickly, preventing structural overload from snow accumulation.

q: 26. The pitched roof which slopes in all the four directions is named as
explain: A hip roof has slopes on all four sides which meet at the corners to form hips.

q: 27. In public buildings the widths of the steps may be kept between
explain: Public buildings require wider stairs (1.5m to 1.8m) to accommodate higher foot traffic and emergency exit requirements.

q: 28. D.P.C. stands for ..........
explain: Damp Proof Course (DPC) is a layer of impervious material (like bitumen or cement) used to prevent moisture from rising up walls.

q: 29. The dampness in the buildings may be caused due to ..........
options: moisture rise in the walls through capillary action
rain beating against external walls and rain travel from wall tops
defective construction such as poor joints in masonry
explain: Dampness can originate from multiple sources including groundwater rise (capillarity), rain penetration, and faulty construction details.

q: 30. A roof which slopes in all the four directions is
explain: A hip roof has slopes on all four sides which meet at the corners to form hips.

q: 31. A roof which slopes in two directions is knows as
explain: A gable roof consists of two sloping surfaces meeting at a ridge, forming a triangle at the ends.

q: 32. The comfortable temperature range in summer may be generally taken as ..........
explain: For human comfort in hot climates, an indoor temperature between 20°C and 25°C is generally considered ideal.

bitumen based material used for water proofing damp proofing etc.
explain: Mastic is a high-viscosity, bitumen-based sealant used for waterproofing joints and DPC.

q: 34. A semi-rigid material ideally suited to make damp proof course is
explain: Mastic asphalt is a semi-rigid, durable material highly effective for preventing dampness.

q: 35. In cinema theaters, to avoid reverberation, the longitudinal walls should be
explain: Walls that converge toward the screen help manage sound reflections and prevent echo.

q: 36. The volume of space per person to be provided in cinema theatres for good acoustics is
explain: Optimal acoustic performance in theaters requires a specific volume (3.7 - 4.2 m2/person) to control sound absorption.

q: 37. The comfortable temperature range in summer may be generally taken as
explain: Human thermal comfort in summer is generally achieved between 20°C and 23°C.

q: 38. Which of the following is true?
options: D.P.C. may be horizontal or vertical
explain: A Damp Proof Course (DPC) must be a continuous, impervious layer and can be applied both horizontally (to stop rising damp) and vertically.

q: 39. In ordinary residential buildings the D.P.C. may be provided ..........
options: between ground level and water table level
explain: DPC is typically provided at the plinth level (usually 15cm to 45cm above ground) to prevent moisture from the soil reaching the walls.

q: 40. The dampness on roof may be due to ..........
explain: Roof dampness often stems from porous tiles/slabs, inadequate overlap of roofing sheets allowing wind-driven rain to enter, or leaking pipes.

q: 41. The most commonly used material for damp proofing is ..........
explain: Bitumen is the most widely used damp-proofing material due to its flexibility, water-repellent nature, and ease of application as a membrane or paint.

q: 42. In case of building without basement, the best position for damp-proof course (D.P.C.) lies at ..........
explain: Providing DPC at the plinth level effectively interrupts the capillary rise of water from the foundation into the superstructure walls.

q: 43. A flexible material used for D.P.C. is ..........
explain: Bitumen sheeting (bituminous felt) is a flexible membrane that can adapt to small structural movements without cracking.

q: 44. The roof having slope in all four directions is called ...........
explain: A hip roof (or hipped roof) has slopes on all four sides which meet at the corners to form 'hips'.

q: 45. Apex line of a sloping roof is called ...........
explain: The ridge is the horizontal peak where two opposing sloping surfaces meet at the top of the roof.

q: 46. Lower edge of the inclined roof surface is called ...........
explain: Eaves (or eves) are the edges of the roof which overhang the face of the wall and normally carry the guttering.

q: 47. The maximum size of aggregate used in D.P.C. is about ...........
explain: For a Damp Proof Course (DPC), which is usually only 2.5cm to 4cm thick, the aggregate size is limited to 10mm to ensure proper compaction and impermeability.

q: 48. In village houses the material used for covering the pitched roof is ...........
explain: Thatch (dried straw, reeds, or grass) is a traditional, locally available roofing material common in rural or village settings.
